# HBarChart

> Native HTML bars with focusable values, selection, and a readable data table.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.9.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HBarChart` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-bar-chart>`.
- Constructor: `HearthBarChartElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Diagrams.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HBarChart.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Native HTML bars, no SVG/canvas/charting dependency. Hover or focus a column to inspect; arrow keys, Home and End move between bars. Activating emits select(id); selected is application-owned. A data-table disclosure provides exact values. Nonfinite/negative values render as zero. Shows the latest maxPoints (default 60, maximum 240). Positive values use a zero baseline scaled to the largest column. Narrow containers scroll internally. --h-chart-1 through --h-chart-5 are color tokens.

## Public API

items: ChartPoint[] · label, description, unit, selected: string · height, maxPoints: number

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    items: ChartPoint[];
    label: string;
    description?: string;
    unit?: string;
    selected?: string;
    height?: number;
    maxPoints?: number;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ items: () => [] }
```

### Events

select(string)

```ts
type Emits = {
    select: [
        id: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, title, viewport, column, segment, tooltip, data, empty

Use `hearth-bar-chart::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface ChartPoint {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    value: number;
}
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HBarChart } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HBarChart label="Build duration" unit="s" :items="[{id:'mon',label:'Mon',value:24},{id:'tue',label:'Tue',value:42},{id:'wed',label:'Wed',value:31}]" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-bar-chart');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Build duration",
  "unit": "s",
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "mon",
      "label": "Mon",
      "value": 24
    },
    {
      "id": "tue",
      "label": "Tue",
      "value": 42
    },
    {
      "id": "wed",
      "label": "Wed",
      "value": 31
    },
    {
      "id": "thu",
      "label": "Thu",
      "value": 18
    },
    {
      "id": "fri",
      "label": "Fri",
      "value": 37
    }
  ]
});

element.addEventListener('select', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
